chapter: Three Deuces and 52nd Street with Tatum
title: Tatum at the Streets of Paris and Lovejoy's; why he thinks Tatum was underrated
summary: He describes the house band and downstairs room, Tatum's seriousness, and his view that Tatum lacked a little showmanship.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: When you were jamming with Fats at Lovejoy's, was he playing at Street of Paris at that time.

Yes yes, he was playing there, he had been there quite a while. Playing a solo. There were two rooms, one was downstairs, one was upstairs. He played at the downstairs room 'cause they had a little a pretty nice band called Big Six... he was the tenor player -- very good, they had a hell of an outfit. But they never got nowhere. They stayed there, they were the house band. He was the house pianist. So, when he would get through, he would go to this after-hours spot cause there wasn't any where else to go. Lovejoy's Big Leg Chicken, that was the name of it.
What was a typical night like when you were at the Streets of Paris?

Average, just average. A lot of celebrities used to come in, you know. But it was such a big room. It was awful big even for the band upstairs it was pretty big. large. But the music lovers, when they came, they came to hear Fats -- So much talk -- Although the man is the most underrated person -- among the underrated that ever was ever alive. I mean too much talent, they got too much talent, they hurt their own selves, looks like. That kind of a thing is possible, you know, you can be too good for your own self. To me if Fats just had a little flash, a little jive, a little whatever. But that wasn't him. He was serious. When he sat down to the piano he played -- there was no clowning. But if he had just had just any little gesture, you might say, that wouldn't have hurt his playing, I mean, look at Earl Garner, he growled more growled more than he played -- haha -- you could hear him growling -- Hamp would be hollering -- Slam, you know? A little gimmick you might say is the only thing in my eyesight that held him back, as far -- Not that he wasn't the greatest piano player in the world, but if he just had a little flashes something to do. Look at Ray Charles -- dances on the piano -- I'm not

talking about the singing part - although he could sing the blues. Excellent. A lot of people didn't know that. He could sing the blues very good. I don't know why he didn't add 'em in there in our little program.
